content.text:
This assembly is worked out from the part geometry, and I did not render it to check it.

- **Wheel fork:** its small top hole sits on the frame's front hole. Its larger axle hole sits on the hub centre, with the axle ahead of and below the pivot.
- **Hub and tyre:** the hub centre and the tyre centre coincide.
- **Tray:** its two end holes (330 px apart) match the frame holes at x≈385 and x≈713, which sets its rotation. The tray is the right way up, with its long sloped wall at the front.
- **Leg stand:** its tip hole goes on the rear frame hole at x≈713. I rotated it so its foot pad and its tip end are level, which makes both ground contacts level.
- **Ground:** the tyre bottom is aligned with the leg's two ground contacts.

Two choices are guesses. I put the leg's tip hole, not its second hole, on the rear frame hole. I also left the frame's larger hole at x≈161 unused. The tip-hole choice is the one that keeps the whole assembly inside the 1376 px width, at about 1360 px.

A single `translate(216,175)` group places the whole assembly on the canvas. The frame is left unrotated.

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1376 768">
  <g transform="translate(216,175)">
    <use href="#kit-tray" transform="translate(149.86,372.08) rotate(249.85)"/>
    <use href="#kit-leg_stand" transform="translate(645.33,60.65) rotate(31.2)"/>
    <use href="#kit-handle_frame"/>
    <use href="#kit-tyre" transform="translate(-211.28,270.32)"/>
    <use href="#kit-wheel_hub" transform="translate(-151.05,330.37)"/>
    <use href="#kit-wheel_fork" transform="translate(-167.10,371.15) rotate(-49.69)"/>
  </g>
</svg>
```
